key_insight: ZFO separates where to move from how far to move: it uses a trusted first-order direction and only a couple of extra function evaluations to choose a curvature-aware step along that direction.
engineering_relevance: This makes LLM fine-tuning more stable and adaptive than fixed-step updates while avoiding the cost of a full line search.
method: Use a first-order optimizer to compute the search direction.
Evaluate the objective at two additional points along that 1D direction.
Fit a local model with shared-sample finite differences to pick a near-optimal step within a bounded interval.
evidence_signal: Across multiple language models and datasets, the method often improved optimization and final performance over fixed-step first-order baselines, with the best local model varying by objective.
watch_item: The approach still depends on the quality of the chosen direction and on accurate finite-difference estimates, so noisy objectives or poor interval settings can reduce reliability.
paper_title: Trust the Direction, Search the Step: Zero-and-First-Order Methods for LLM Fine-Tuning
